evidence.title: Factories, Farms and Material Suppliers
evidence.supportingText: [Excerpt pending verification] Patagonia's supply-chain disclosure page; per search-index snippets it describes 'due diligence activities to promote and sustain fair labor practices, safe working conditions and environmental responsibility in the finished-goods factories, farms and material suppliers', including a Material Traceability program, and links a directory of supply-chain partners in countries including Taiwan, Vietnam, India and Nicaragua. patagonia.com returned a 404/anti-bot placeholder to automated fetches, so no verbatim excerpt could be captured.

evidence.title: Open Supply Hub
evidence.supportingText: Open Supply Hub (OS Hub) is an accessible, collaborative, supply chain mapping platform, used and populated by stakeholders across sectors and supply chains.

events.evidenceSummary: Patagonia documents an organic-cotton program and discloses its farms and material suppliers at the program level, but it does not disclose growing countries per product; the cotton in this specific shirt cannot be tied to a country or farm from public records. The most recent machine-readable supplier list found is from May 2020, and its staleness is reflected in its reliability score.
Patagonia discloses its factory list but does not publicly map products to factories; identifying the factory would require the style's Footprint data or item-level traceability.

events.inferenceBasis: Patagonia's disclosed finished-goods factories are predominantly outside the US, per the company's contributed factory list mirrored on Open Supply Hub, so a US-market unit of this style almost certainly entered the country as an import; no customs or shipment record ties this style to a specific vessel, port or entry date.
events.evidenceSummary: US import is inferred rather than documented: the structured copy of Patagonia's factory disclosure shows finished-goods production concentrated abroad, but no public record links this style to a specific import shipment or port of entry.
